0.0.n: A polite way to address a group, with さん adding respect.

0.2.n: A neutral, polite way to refer to yourself.

0.3.n: Marks 私 as the topic: the speaker is talking about themselves.

1.0.n: This is the first part of イヤホン, split here; it is not a separate word.

1.1.n: This is the second part of イヤホン; the whole word names the listening device.

1.2.n: Shows that イヤホン is what the speaker bought.

1.3.n: Polite past form of 買う, used for a completed purchase.

2.0.n: This is the first part of イヤホン, split here; it is not a separate word.

2.1.n: This is the second part of イヤホン; read both parts together as one word.

2.2.n: Marks the earphones as what was bought, with the verb coming in the next line.

2.4.n: Together with つ, this forms 1つ, read ひとつ.

2.5.n: Combines with 1 to count one item or set without specifying its type.

2.7.n: Together with つ, this forms 2つ, read ふたつ.

2.8.n: Combines with 2 to count two items or sets, here earphones.

3.0.n: Together with つ, this forms 2つ, read ふたつ.

3.1.n: Counts the earphones as two items or sets, not necessarily two individual earpieces.

3.2.n: Polite past form of 買う; the quantity 2つ comes directly before it.

4.0.n: Here it serves as a brief acknowledgment before the speaker continues.

4.2.n: With a negative verb, it shows that the action has not happened up to now.

4.3.n: 開ける becomes 開けて plus いません, a polite negative describing an action not yet done.

0.tip: は introduces the speaker as the topic, and the sentence continues into the next line.

1.tip: 買いました is polite past tense; the subject is already supplied by 私は in the previous line.

2.tip: 1つ and 2つ use the general counting forms ひとつ and ふたつ.

3.tip: つ is a general counter; here it counts sets of earphones rather than explicitly saying pairs.

4.tip: まだ with ていません expresses that something has not happened yet.
